mechanism_narrative: A one percentage point increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with a negative 20-day return on the S&P 500, as higher unemployment signals weaker economic conditions and reduced corporate earnings growth potential, leading to lower equity valuations.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 0.5%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates and stimulates economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 6.5% and the monthly change in employment (PAYEMS) is negative (growth rate < 0.2% over 3 months), it indicates a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both conditions are met (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 2.5%), a federal funds rate above 1.0% signals a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both conditions are met (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 600,000 units (600 in thousands), it signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below 600 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2% (as measured by GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 0.2%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy that leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105 and residential sales (RSAFS) falls below 340,000 million dollars, it indicates a simultaneous slowdown in manufacturing and housing demand, reducing economic activity and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both conditions are met (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.05.
